date: 19th century (notebook kept c. 1817-1898; the cipher entries are by Muhammad 'Ali al-Hamdani, 1833-1898)
title: Hamdani family scrapbook: notes in Muhammad 'Ali al-Hamdani's private cipher (fol. 83b) and a list of imams 'much of it in cipher' (fol. 29a-b)
correspondents: Muhammad 'Ali al-Hamdani (compiler); private notes, no addressee
place: India (Surat) and the Hejaz/Yemen journeys of the compiler; not stated in the record
shelfmark: London, Institute of Ismaili Studies, MS 1662 [Handlist 105] (Hamdani Collection)
folio_note: 104 ff., 19 x 14.5 cm. fol. 83b: 'Notes written in the same system of cipher that Muhammad 'Ali used in Ms. 1499'; fol. 29a-b: 'List of the imams down to al-Tayyib, with some biographical information, much of it in cipher'; fol. 21a: opening of a letter 'in cipher (not the usual secret script, but there is an indubitably correct decipherment above each letter)' (that one is read); fol. 23a: 'the letters of the usual secret script in alphabetical order' (a key)
status: de Blois's catalogue (2011), as given on the IIS online record, reads the fol. 21a cipher line and quotes it, but gives no reading for the fol. 83b notes or the enciphered parts of fol. 29a-b. The system of fol. 83b is that of IIS MS 1499, a whole copy of Kanz al-walad in an 'invented script' which de Blois says is 'a straightforward cipher' crackable against the printed text (ed. Ghalib 1971): the key can be rebuilt from MS 1499, but no reading of fol. 83b is on record. Not on DECODE (searched 'Hamdani', 'Ismaili', 'Arabic': 0 records). Not viewed: no images online.
why: Private notes of a 19th-century Tayyibi Ismaili scholar that he chose to hide even inside a family notebook; next to them the same notebook holds a rival list of hidden imams.
score_note: Scored from the catalogue description during the 15 Nov 2026 Arabic sweep, part D (research/sweep_2026-11-15_arabic/part_D.md); not viewed
verify: Ask the IIS for images of MS 1662 fols 29a-b and 83b and of a few pages of MS 1499; check de Blois 2011 in print (entry for Ms. 1662 and the introduction on secret script) for any reading of fol. 83b; align MS 1499 with Ghalib's edition of Kanz al-walad for the key.

title: Tayyibi cosmological treatise 'Risalat [falak al-qamar?]' with part of the text in a cryptic alphabet
place: unknown (Yemeni Tayyibi tradition; Indian Bohra copy)
shelfmark: London, Institute of Ismaili Studies, MS 1291 (ArI, ZA)(b) (Zahid 'Ali Collection)
folio_note: ff. 71r-86v, 12 lines a page; 'part of the text in cryptic alphabet; defective at the beginning' (amount not stated)
status: Cortese's catalogue (2003), as given on the IIS online record, notes the cryptic alphabet and gives no reading; the title itself is the cataloguer's conjecture. Most cipher in Tayyibi manuscripts is the community's standard secret script, whose alphabet is in print (Strothmann 1943; de Blois 1984 and 2011; a table on fol. 1a of IIS MS 1455 and on fol. 23a of MS 1662), so this is probably a lookup once images exist; that it is the standard script is not stated in the record. Not on DECODE. Not viewed: no images online.
why: An unidentified Tayyibi treatise whose hidden passages may name the persons or doctrines the copyist thought dangerous; reading them could identify the work.
